{
  "research_question": "How do the five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a One-Way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "Test the null hypothesis that the mean performance for each metric is equal across all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Calculate F-statistics and p-values to determine if significant variance exists between group means.",
    "Check homogeneity of variances (Levene's Test) prior to ANOVA execution."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If ANOVA indicates significant effects (p < 0.05), conduct pairwise comparisons between all 10 possible pairs of stimulation paradigms.",
    "Calculate mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for each pair.",
    "Report adjusted p-values to account for multiple testing.",
    "Identify specific paradigm pairs driving the overall group differences."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Bonferroni correction",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Since the response variables are continuous and the predictor (Stim Paradigm) is categorical, a One-Way ANOVA (equivalent to a linear model with dummy coding) is appropriate. However, for the 'Success' variable which is binary (0 or 1), a Logistic Regression (Generalized Linear Model with binomial link) is explicitly recommended over Ordinary Least Squares to ensure valid inference and probability bounds.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality of residuals: Verify via Shapiro-Wilk test or Q-Q plots for each response variable.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Verify via Levene's test across the five paradigms.",
    "Independence of observations: Assumed based on experimental design (n=76655 rows).",
    "Linearity: Not applicable for categorical predictors, but linearity of means is assumed.",
    "Outlier detection: Inspect residuals for extreme values, noting the wide range in Path Efficiency (0.0009 to 29.8)."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency) compared to 'Sham' due to multimodal stimulation.",
    "Significant differences are expected between 'ICMS Only' and 'Dim Visual Only' versus 'Bright Visual Only', reflecting the specific sensory inputs.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in 'Combined' and highest in 'Sham', indicating better path straightness with multimodal input.",
    "Average Speed may show an inverse relationship with AD, where more efficient paths correlate with higher sustained speeds.",
    "Success rates may vary significantly, with 'Combined' potentially approaching ceiling effects while 'Sham' shows lower rates."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset contains 8 distinct mouse IDs (levels), but the ANOVA treats 'Stim Paradigm' as the sole factor; individual mouse variability (random effect) is not explicitly modeled, potentially inflating Type I error if mice are nested within paradigms non-randomly.",
    "Extreme outliers in 'Path Efficiency' (max 29.8 vs mean 0.47) may violate ANOVA assumptions of normality and homoscedasticity, requiring robust statistical methods or data transformation.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption of standard ANOVA, necessitating a Generalized Linear Model (Logistic Regression) instead.",
    "Unbalanced design: The number of trials per paradigm varies significantly (e.g., Combined=48846 vs Sham=3505), which can affect power and variance estimates."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a Mixed-Effects Model (Linear Mixed Model or Generalized Linear Mixed Model) treating 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for inter-individual variability, and re-run the analysis with the appropriate distribution (Gaussian for most metrics, Binomial for Success) to obtain more rigorous p-values and effect sizes."
}
